content.text:
I fixed the SSRF issue with a one-line change at `lib/adapters/http.js:232`:

```js
const parsed = new URL(fullPath, platform.hasBrowserEnv ? platform.origin : undefined);
```

Before, the Node HTTP adapter always parsed request URLs against `http://localhost`. That is how `//google.com` was turned into `http://google.com/` even when a `baseURL` was set. On the server there is now no fallback base. A protocol-relative URL like the one in the issue fails with `ERR_INVALID_URL` instead of being sent to another host. In a browser environment, the page's origin is still used as the base.

**Side effect:** this also brings back the pre-1.3.2 behaviour for plain relative paths. In Node, a request like `axios.get('/foo')` with no `baseURL` will now fail with `ERR_INVALID_URL`, which is the behaviour that #5458 had changed. Requests that set a `baseURL` are unaffected.

**Testing:**
- I ran the issue's case (a `baseURL` plus `get('//google.com')`) and it now throws `ERR_INVALID_URL`.
- In `test/unit/adapters/http.js`, 109 tests pass and 2 fail. Both failures are rate-limit tests that time out after 2 seconds, and they fail the same way with my change removed. I didn't add a regression test.
